edges.qualification: Construction and maintenance work contribute to operating reconstructed fields; no particular labour organisation is asserted to be uniquely necessary.

scope.configuration: Modern reconstructed raised fields assessed over crop rotations rather than a first harvest.

alternatives: Different field designs or maintenance schedules
Dryland cropping with different labour requirements
edges.dispute: Bandy's labour accounting is schematic and inherits heterogeneous studies; it does not establish net superiority or universal infeasibility.

edges.qualification: Raised-field and dryland rotations can be competing uses of cultivation effort; comparison depends on land/water suitability and time horizon.

scope.configuration: Titicaca agricultural comparisons with fallow, maintenance and seed quality relevant to the denominator.

alternatives: Mixed portfolios of raised and dryland fields
edges.dispute: The alternatives are not interchangeable at every site; some reported comparisons favour raised fields and per-hectare goals may differ from per-workday goals.

edges.qualification: Canal water contributes to drainage/water-management and local heat-exchange functions in reconstructed blocks; magnitude depends on design and conditions.

scope.configuration: Erickson's small reconstructed blocks, with two reported frost-night observations.

alternatives: Other drainage or frost-management practices; equal effectiveness not established
edges.dispute: No basin-scale seasonal average or ancient effect size is inferred from two nights; water level and plot location may confound comparisons.

edges.qualification: The documented local institutions provide a route for agreement on calendars; no unique institutional necessity or optimal historical origin is claimed.

scope.configuration: Temple/subak-linked calendars in the Oos–Petanu account and the observed 1988–1989 Manuaba configuration.

alternatives: Other cooperative or administrative calendar-setting institutions
edges.dispute: Janssen's historical narrative inherits Lansing; model reanalysis does not independently identify how institutions originated or compare enforcement costs.

edges.qualification: Coordination can manage pest–water interactions; this is not a claim that universal synchronisation maximises actual harvests.

scope.configuration: The observed/modelled connected rice fields under stated pest dynamics, water limits and decision rules.

alternatives: Coordinated staggering where water limits dominate
Independent schedules where external interactions are weak
edges.dispute: Simulated benefit is conditional; aggregate harvest and distribution across subaks differ, and real ecological parameters require independent measurement.

edges.qualification: Modern varieties and temple-linked coordination coexist in a documented crop calendar; coexistence does not estimate the separate benefit of either component.

scope.configuration: Manuaba's 1988–1989 coordinated calendar with improved rice varieties, including IR64.

alternatives: Other rice-variety mixes compatible with local scheduling
edges.dispute: No Bali-wide seed-retention share, universal compatibility or head-to-head yield effect is inferred.

edges.qualification: Shared limited water makes simultaneous demand a possible constraint; its importance relative to pest pressure varies.

scope.configuration: Oos–Petanu model/field setting in which irrigation demands interact through shared flows.

alternatives: Less water-demanding crop choices, not evaluated here
edges.dispute: This does not prove water scarcity caused institutional formation or the same schedule is preferred at every parameter value.

edges.qualification: Negotiated returns can support labour cooperation in the project; the evidence is qualitative and does not isolate a contract effect.

scope.configuration: Women cultivators' participation, compensation and crop-control negotiations in Jahaly-Pacharr communities.

edges.dispute: Outside options, political connections and operating conditions vary alongside compensation; not every participant has the same bargaining position.

edges.qualification: Uncompensated obligations with weak control of returns can reduce labour cooperation; not all project decline is attributed to this channel.

scope.configuration: Project plots under household control where women supplying labour have competing independently controlled opportunities.

alternatives: Lower use when alternative crops are more rewarding
edges.dispute: Fuel, machinery, input prices and marketing also deteriorated; no causal fraction of yield decline is identified.

edges.qualification: Other crops compete for labour and can make lower irrigated-rice utilisation rational at household or individual level.

scope.configuration: Jahaly-Pacharr households with rainfed/upland alternatives, especially when rainfall or control of returns changes their relative value.

alternatives: Paid labour supply rather than own-plot cultivation
edges.dispute: Rights to alternatives differ among cultivators. The early IFPRI and later Carney accounts do not form a common causal panel.

edges.qualification: Women's groups adapt to supplying paid farm labour, one route to labour provision under changed incentives.

scope.configuration: Paid agricultural-group activity described in the project communities, distinct from uncompensated family obligations.

edges.dispute: No universal prevalence or estimated productivity effect of the groups is available; adaptation does not prove all women benefit.

edges.qualification: Fuel, parts and input/service availability support continued operation; their failures are documented alongside labour conflicts.

scope.configuration: Pump/machinery/input package in Jahaly-Pacharr during the later operating difficulties described by Carney.

alternatives: Tidal or rainfed systems with different operating requirements
edges.dispute: The report does not isolate individual supply failures or claim these inputs guarantee profitable operation.

edges.qualification: Local adaptation can make internationally developed breeding material useful in particular crops/environments; there is no universal same-package requirement.

scope.configuration: Modern-variety diffusion in the environments discussed by Pingali's retrospective.

alternatives: Other breeding programmes or locally developed cultivars
Existing varieties adapted to marginal environments
edges.dispute: A review supplies mechanism context, not a clean estimate of the contribution of national adaptation separate from policy and inputs.

edges.qualification: Suitable water and input systems support realised benefits for some varieties; irrigation is explicitly not a universal prerequisite for improved seed.

scope.configuration: Crop/environment-specific modern-variety packages in favourable versus marginal production environments.

alternatives: Alternative crops suited to available resources
edges.dispute: Public investment, prices, access and research targeting can cause both complement availability and uptake; components are not individually identified.

edges.qualification: Withdrawals exceeding replenishment are the study's likely explanation for regional groundwater depletion; there is no edge assigning a seed-specific causal share.

scope.configuration: Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana including Delhi, August 2002–October 2008, with GRACE storage estimates and modelled component subtraction.

alternatives: A rival explanation through other storage changes was examined, not assumed absent
edges.dispute: Regional component uncertainty remains; no current/all-India rate or separate policy, seed and pumping effects are asserted.

edges.qualification: More secure control can increase the expected captured return to waiting and support longer fallow; formal individual title is not asserted to be uniquely necessary.

scope.configuration: Plots and cultivators in the two-year Akwapim survey and retrospective plot histories.

alternatives: Different credible collective or individual rights arrangements
edges.dispute: Observational/IV interpretation depends on exclusions; political status may affect other productive resources.

edges.qualification: Local political position is associated with more secure practical control, including during fallow; it is not a universal law of landholding.

scope.configuration: Akwapim local land arrangements where status and plot-acquisition route vary among and within cultivators.

alternatives: Secure control through different acquisition routes
edges.dispute: Power, wealth, labour access and plot selection are not fully separable; gender differences cannot be assigned to one pathway with certainty.

edges.qualification: Randomly offered insurance increases investment under the tested contracts, without proving universal credit sufficiency or welfare improvement.

scope.configuration: Northern Ghana 2009–2011 cash/insurance experiment and its sampled farmers.

alternatives: Cash grants with different observed responses
edges.dispute: Insurance and cash differ in state contingency, value and timing; the precise decomposition of insurance effects is not complete.

edges.qualification: Payment credibility is one candidate explanation for payout-sensitive demand, not an independently established unique psychological mechanism.

scope.configuration: Ghana trial participants' later demand under varying prices and observed payout/network experience.

alternatives: Better matching between rainfall index and individual loss
Lower premium or different payment timing
Rational learning about contract value rather than distrust
edges.dispute: Basis risk, recency and rational learning can predict similar demand; independent credibility and index-quality interventions are needed.

edges.qualification: Continued use and repair shape the functioning of the offered stove; mediator effects are not separately randomised.

scope.configuration: Low-cost improved biomass stove with household upkeep responsibility over up to four years of follow-up.

edges.dispute: Meal needs, inherent emissions performance and other pollution sources can also limit exposure effects; blaming users is not an identified mechanism.

edges.qualification: Older stoves remain in use and compete for cooking tasks; ownership of an improved device is not complete displacement of biomass exposure.

scope.configuration: Mixed cooking-device use recorded during the Odisha programme's follow-up.

alternatives: A different cooking package fitting household requirements
edges.dispute: The reasons for each household's stacking are not uniquely identified; continued use may reflect practical fit, cost or preferences.

edges.qualification: Fuel delivery, instruction and support are documented components of the randomised high-adherence package, not independently estimated necessary components.

scope.configuration: Selected sites in Guatemala, India, Peru and Rwanda during 2018–2020 recruitment and pregnancy follow-up.

alternatives: Commercial fuel delivery with unknown uptake in this trial
edges.dispute: The package is bundled and free; no component effect, unsubsidised demand or post-support persistence is identified.

edges.qualification: Appliances contribute to household production while output, standards, services and work allocation change; no aggregate causal hours effect is inferred.

scope.configuration: Cowan's mainly middle-class early-twentieth-century account, interpreted alongside Ramey's broader time-use reconstruction.

edges.dispute: Historical documentation and reconstructed hours are not independent appliance assignment; early and later populations differ.

edges.qualification: Some early machines still require attendance and manual handling; lower exertion need not imply unattended operation.

scope.configuration: Operating examples described by Cowan, including early washing-machine work, not every appliance through 2005.

alternatives: Other devices with more automatic operation
edges.dispute: The examples establish remaining operations, not their national frequency or a uniform absence of time savings.

edges.qualification: Changing service standards may accompany appliance use and absorb some technical gains in greater output; this is a candidate demand-adjustment mechanism.

scope.configuration: Early-twentieth-century US historical interpretation and a proposed accounting explanation for divergent hours/output trends.

alternatives: Fixed-output tasks with direct time savings
Demographic or domestic-service changes explaining hours independently
edges.dispute: Cowan qualifies advertising/standard causation. Neither source identifies a national rebound magnitude or proves standards were caused by appliances.

edges.qualification: Hired labour and purchased services are alternatives to some appliance-mediated household operations, with unequal access and possible coexistence.

scope.configuration: Cowan's middle-class household context where domestic service and machine operation are reorganised.

edges.dispute: No one-for-one domestic-worker displacement coefficient or appliance-specific employment effect is estimated.

edges.qualification: Leaving a plot fallow longer competes with earlier recultivation, which can help retain a practical claim at a productivity cost.

scope.configuration: Akwapim fallow timing under different practical security and acquisition routes.

alternatives: More secure control enabling longer fallow
edges.dispute: The observed tradeoff does not eliminate cash, labour or plot-quality constraints and does not imply every short fallow is a tenure response.

semantics: Scoped typed multigraph. No edge is transitive across episodes. Empty joint_inputs means no bundle claim, not sufficiency. The disconnected ancient-field node deliberately avoids asserting transmission from ancient use to modern revival. No seed-specific edge to groundwater depletion is supported.
